artists.biography: Easy Star All-Stars is a reggae collective with a rotating roster of musicians and singers founded by the co-founders (Michael Goldwasser, Eric Smith, Lem Oppenheimer & Remy Gerstein) of New York City-based Easy Star Records in 1997. They originally formed as a studio band for the label's earliest recordings. Although they have backed many artists[who?] and produced several original releases, they are best known for covering popular albums in a reggae and dub style and have released four cover albums to date. The first, released in 2003, was an interpretation of Pink Floyd's classic The Dark Side of the Moon entitled Dub Side of the Moon; the second was 2006's Radiodread, a song-by-song cover of Radiohead's OK Computer. In April 2009, they released a cover of The Beatles' Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band entitled Easy Star's Lonely Hearts Dub Band. In 2012, Easy Star's Thrillah was released, a cover of Michael Jackson's classic album. In March 2008 they released an EP consisting mostly of non-cover material. On 5 April 2011, they released their first original album entitled First Light.

perplexity.description:
Dubber Side of the Moon by Easy Star All-Stars, released on October 25, 2010, is a dub remix album that reimagines their 2003 reggae tribute Dub Side of the Moon, itself a reinterpretation of Pink Floyd’s The Dark Side of the Moon. This album features bass-heavy dub remixes crafted by a diverse group of prominent dub producers from around the world, including Dubmatix, Mad Professor, Adrian Sherwood, and others. The result is a trippier, more atmospheric version that extends the original’s reggae and dub roots into deeper, more experimental dub and dubstep territories, emphasizing heavy basslines and echo effects characteristic of the dub genre.

Positioned as a follow-up and expansion of the band’s breakthrough 2003 release, Dubber Side of the Moon showcases Easy Star All-Stars’ continued innovation in blending electronic and reggae styles. While Dub Side of the Moon had already achieved critical acclaim and commercial success—remaining on the Billboard reggae charts for over seven years and earning praise from outlets like Rolling Stone and NPR—Dubber Side of the Moon was welcomed as an essential dub companion that further solidified the band’s reputation as fearless pioneers in reggae reinterpretations. It debuted at number two on the Billboard Reggae charts and received positive reviews for its adventurous remix approach. The album was released on Easy Star Records, the band’s own label, maintaining their independent and artist-driven ethos.
